text.p: Italian bond futures gunned to another historic high in late trade as European monetary union hopes and general positive sentiment in bonds lit the fuse of investor buying.
The December futures contract on LIFFE rocketed to a fresh record of 125.80 and stood 192 basis points up on the day at 125.62 by 1640 GMT.

"I though we were going to stop at 125.00, but everyone was buying," said one broker in London. The July 2006 Btp broke the 8.0 percent yield barrier to end at 7.88 percent and the spread over the 10-year Bund ratcheted past 200 basis points to 195.
Dealers said U.S. hedge funds set off the first fireworks of the day when the Btp future broke chart levels this morning.

Comments from French President Jacques Chirac that he had no doubt Spain would join a single European currency at its start and would like to see Italy there as well gave a further boost. Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar gave Btps a fillip when he said Spain wanted Italy to be in EMU from the first moment.

Bund strength on the successful completion of Russian President Yeltsin's heart operation proved a spur to bonds and traders said buying had also been strong as concern faded that Democrats would take control of Congress in U.S. elections.

"It's difficult to say what level comes next," said one broker in London. "I wouldn't be surprised to see a correction after the U.S. elections results. But the 124.00 area on the Btp future looks like it will be a good base."

On the domestic front Wednesday brings Italy's final consumer prices data for October which are forecast to show a year on year rate of 3.0 percent. The European Commission is also likely to release its bi-annual economic forecasts.
